summary.intent: Plan and execute GSD roadmap phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end — research, scope resolution, planning, verification, and wave-based execution — then spin up an independent worktree to start phase 69 in parallel.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed fully (research, Nyquist VALIDATION.md, D-07 full-boundary scope decision, pattern map, REQUIREMENTS registration, 12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, coverage gates green) and committed; execution began sequentially on the main tree and completed Waves 1-3 (plans 01, 02, 03) with all tests green and two tracking corrections applied. A second git worktree was created off origin/main for independent phase 69 work, with instructions handed to the user to kick off discuss-phase/plan-phase there.

repo: cipher-box is a pnpm monorepo; worktree executors need their own `pnpm install` per worktree, which is expensive — for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is preferred over parallel worktrees.

GSD worktree base-check exposes `shouldDegrade` and `worktree.baseRef` (e.g. 'head' vs 'fresh'/origin-main) — must verify baseRef is 'head' before dispatching worktree executors, otherwise they'd fork from origin/main and miss uncommitted-to-main PLAN.md files.

Executors sometimes prematurely mark REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes ([x]) complete when only a partial slice of the requirement's acceptance criteria is done (e.g., SDK-READ-01/02 marked complete in Wave 1/2 even though full satisfaction requires deleting old web services in Wave 6) — orchestrator must cross-check checkbox state against full AC text, not just trust the executor.

packages/sdk/src/folder-listing.ts's `resolveChildren` intentionally skips (omits) any child that fails resolve/unseal rather than erroring the whole listing, but does NOT swallow the folder-level ROT-07 gate — the target folder is already gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs, so the trust boundary holds even with graceful per-child degradation.

The gap-analysis post-planning check (`gap-analysis.plan-post`) can emit control characters in its `rendered` field that break the orchestrator's normal parser — running the check directly (bypassing the wrapper) is the workaround.

code.finding: Docstring documents the security reasoning for why per-child skip-on-failure in resolveChildren is safe: target folder already gated before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is omitted rather than rendered with stale/attacker content.
New ROT-07 anti-rollback gate call site added on the root resolve path (resolvePublishedNode) as part of Plan 68.2-01.
New ROT-07 gate call site added inside the dfsFindFolder child loop, alongside the pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.

workflow: For security-critical waves, independently re-run the acceptance/gate tests rather than trusting the subagent executor's self-reported pass — used to confirm Wave 1's ROT-07 gate and Wave 2's deviation before advancing.

When an executor reports a 'notable deviation' (e.g. widened error handling) on security-adjacent code, read the actual implementation and re-run the relevant security tests before accepting the change, rather than accepting the executor's own justification at face value.

When a scope ambiguity surfaces mid-workflow (e.g. D-07's literal wording sweeping in unrelated files), pause and use AskUserQuestion to lock the resolution into CONTEXT.md before the planner runs, rather than letting the planner guess.

Before creating a worktree for parallel independent work, verify the target phase's roadmap 'depends on' note is a design-mirroring dependency rather than a hard code dependency, since that changes whether the worktree needs cross-branch reference docs copied in.

friction: The GSD commit-helper `commit_failed` false negative (already known/documented) recurred multiple times during this session, requiring manual `git log` verification after nearly every commit step.
The post-planning gap-analysis check's parser choked on control characters in the `rendered` field, forcing a direct/manual invocation of the underlying check.
`git fetch` failed entirely from the sandboxed session (no network access to GitHub), requiring reliance on a cached local origin/main ref and manual reasoning to confirm it was still current.

Multiple executors (Wave 1 and Wave 2) independently marked REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes complete before the full acceptance criteria (old service deletion) were actually satisfied, requiring manual detection and correction by the orchestrator across two separate spot-checks.
open_items: D-03's poll-invalidation leg has no dedicated automated test (only a call-site grep) — logged as todo `.planning/todos/pending/2026-07-06-d03-poll-invalidation-lacks-automated-coverage.md` for follow-up gap closure.
Offered but not yet done: copying phase 68.2's CONTEXT.md/RESEARCH.md into the new phase-69 worktree as design-mirroring reference material.

Phase 69 worktree still needs `/gsd-discuss-phase 69` (recommended first, due to a required grant-root scope design pass and an unresolved FUSE delete-authority-model question) before planning/execution can start.
Phase 69 worktree has no node_modules/cargo target yet — `cargo fetch`/`cargo build` and `pnpm install` needed before any Rust build/test there.

Phase 68.2 execution: Waves 4-7 (plans 04,06,07,08,09,10,11,12) not yet executed — remaining work includes web rewire, off-path pocket cutover, deleting 4 orphaned services with the D-07 grep gate, and the final SealedChildRef mirror revert + full web-e2e gate.
